newsitem.title: UK: Northern Ireland police escape guerrilla rocket.
newsitem.headline: Northern Ireland police escape guerrilla rocket.

text.p: Suspected IRA guerrillas fired a rocket at a Belfast police patrol on Thursday night in what British officials called a "discouraging" development after British Prime Minister Tony Blair's new peace initiative.

The attack, in which no one was injured, came less than 36 hours after Blair unveiled a new formula designed to allow the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, to enter into all-party talks on the future of the province.
"They (Sinn Fein) have to decide whether or not they join substantive talks," an official in Blair's Downing Street office said on Friday.
"Obviously events like last night are discouraging in that respect."
Northern Irish police said the rocket was launched at an armoured Landrover which had slowed down near a school.
"The projectile missed the Landrover and struck a corner wall of the school. No member of the Landrover crew was injured," a spokesman said.

No group claimed responsibility. But security sources said the weapon was a type often used by Irish Republican Army guerrillas who have waged a 28-year-campaign to end British rule in Northern Ireland and merge it with the Irish Republic.

British security forces had been on alert for IRA attacks after two police officers were shot dead in the town of Lurgan on June 16. On Wednesday police foiled guerrilla plans for an ambush on a security patrol in south Belfast.

The rocket was fired in a flashpoint zone where tension has been high for months between Roman Catholic nationalists and Protestant loyalists. Northern Ireland's Protestant majority favours continued ties with Britain.
